title: Repository and Service Patterns knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is the strongest evidence that an application design is ready for review?
options: A large number of abstractions without tests.
Only a screenshot of the happy path.
A successful compile with no runtime checks or acceptance criteria.
Clear domain contracts, implemented behavior, tests for normal and failure cases, and reproducible setup/documentation.
questions.answer_key: Clear domain contracts, implemented behavior, tests for normal and failure cases, and reproducible setup/documentation.
questions.explanation: Production-oriented work is supported by explicit acceptance criteria and repeatable evidence.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Repository and Service Patterns”?
options: A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with data access abstractions and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with data access abstractions and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Data access abstractions”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Repository and Service Patterns”?
options: Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check business logic services, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume typed boundaries between application layers is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Check business logic services, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Business logic services”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
